hints: Notice sound is a longitudinal wave carried by vibrating air particles, so think what happens if there are no particles in a vacuum.
Recall polarisation only restricts the plane of transverse oscillations, so ask whether sound oscillations are transverse or parallel to travel.
Recall diffraction through a gap happens for all types of wave when the gap width is similar to the wavelength.
walkthrough: Identify sound as a longitudinal progressive wave where air particles oscillate parallel to the direction of energy transfer by compressions and rarefactions.
For travel in a vacuum: with no particles there is nothing to compress, so sound requires a solid, liquid or gas and the entry is no.
For polarisation: only transverse waves can be polarised because only they have oscillations perpendicular to travel that can be restricted to one plane, so for longitudinal sound the entry is no.
For diffraction: all waves spread out after passing through a gap of order the wavelength, and sound is heard around doorways, so the entry is yes.
The row no, no, yes matches the table row for A. This is option A.

A.explanation: Sound needs a medium for compressions and rarefactions, cannot be polarised as it is longitudinal, but can diffract like all waves.

B.explanation: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum and it does diffract through a gap, so both the first and third columns are wrong.

C.explanation: Sound is longitudinal so it cannot be polarised, and it can diffract, so the second and third columns are wrong.

D.explanation: Sound cannot be polarised because its oscillations are parallel to travel, although it can diffract.
